newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy lira seen joining ERM at around 1,000/mark.
newsitem.headline: Italy lira seen joining ERM at around 1,000/mark.

text.p: The lira is seen entering Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism with a central parity of around 1,000 per mark, a Reuter poll of 13 analysts showed on Wednesday.

"The re-entry levels for the Finnish markka in the ERM were very close to the average market prices in the last six months. The same thing could happen for the lira," said Gregorio De Felice, economist at Banca Commericiale Italiana.

"Today the mark/lira six-months average is at 1,012. In one month's time, if the lira stabilizes at current rates, the average will be of 1,008 and by the end of December at 1,005. I see a central parity close to 1,000 per mark," De Felice added.

Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio on October 10 told the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) budget commission that the lira was not that far off what he called its equilibrium point. On that day the lira was trading in a 993-998 per mark range.
Most analysts see the lira returning to the currency grid by the end of the year.

"At the end of next month, the lower house will already have approved the 1997 budget law, clearing the way for an interest rate cut. These are two prerequisites for the lira's re-entry into the ERM," an analyst at Bank of America in Milan said.
Following are the results of the poll:
1. When will the lira return to the Exchange Rate Mechanism?
At the end of November 4 out of 13
By the end of the year 5/13
2. What will be the lira's central parity in the ERM?

Institutions surveyed were: Banca di Roma, Bank of America, Chase Manhattan, BCI, Credit, NatWest, San Paolo Bank, Indosuez, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank. Two others took part but declined to be quoted.
